# Marmot

> Marmot is an open protocol for decentralized, end-to-end encrypted group messaging. It uses Messaging Layer Security (MLS) for group encryption and Nostr public keys for identity. Current clients use Nostr relays for transport.

MDK is the Rust implementation and provides MarmotKit native bindings, a C interface, and the White Noise runtime. Marmot TypeScript is a separate implementation for JavaScript and TypeScript applications. White Noise is a messenger built on Marmot. The guides below follow the latest stable releases and link to their version-pinned sources.

## Protocol and ecosystem

- [Marmot protocol specification](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/marmot): Protocol and interoperability requirements.
- [White Noise](https://www.whitenoise.chat/): End-user messenger and downloads.

## Start here

- [Documentation](https://marmot.build/docs/index.md): Find the right Marmot developer guide for native apps, Rust, C, TypeScript, the command line, or agent integrations.

## Integration guides

- [Native apps · MarmotKit](https://marmot.build/docs/native-apps.md): Integrate MarmotKit into iOS, macOS, or Android apps and use its native bindings for encrypted messaging, groups, and account management.
- [Rust application runtime](https://marmot.build/docs/rust-runtime.md): Use the Rust application runtime to manage Marmot accounts, messaging, storage, and networking in a Rust application.
- [C and native hosts](https://marmot.build/docs/c-interface.md): Integrate Marmot into a native host through its C ABI, from building the library to calling it and managing its handles.
- [Bots and agents](https://marmot.build/docs/agents.md): Connect a bot or coding agent to White Noise over a local control socket and manage its messaging permissions.
- [Terminal and scripts](https://marmot.build/docs/cli.md): Set up the White Noise CLI and use terminal commands or scripts to manage accounts, groups, and encrypted messages.
- [TypeScript quickstart](https://marmot.build/docs/typescript.md): Install the Marmot TypeScript SDK, connect a client to Nostr, and start sending end-to-end encrypted group messages.
- [TypeScript storage](https://marmot.build/docs/typescript-storage.md): Choose and configure Marmot TypeScript storage for browser or server applications, including how to plug in custom storage.
- [TypeScript networking](https://marmot.build/docs/typescript-network.md): Connect Marmot TypeScript clients to Nostr relays and configure the transport for sending and receiving group events.

## Reference

- [MarmotKit distribution](https://marmot.build/docs/distribution.md): Choose and install the published MarmotKit packages for Apple and Android platforms, or build the native bindings from source.
- [MarmotKit API](https://marmot.build/docs/native-api.md): Look up MarmotKit methods and types for accounts, encrypted messaging, groups, media, and other operations in native apps.
- [C API](https://marmot.build/docs/c-api.md): Look up Marmot’s C functions and types, including calling conventions, return values, and ownership requirements.
- [Architecture](https://marmot.build/docs/architecture.md): Explore how the Marmot Development Kit organizes MLS group state, encrypted storage, Nostr relay access, and client runtimes.
- [Upgrade guide](https://marmot.build/docs/upgrading.md): Review version-specific breaking changes and migration steps before upgrading an application to the latest stable MDK release.

## Optional

- [Marmot apps](https://marmot.build/apps.html): Apps built on the protocol.
- [Release notes](https://marmot.build/updates.html): Published MDK and Marmot TypeScript changes.
